items.title: Package scripts cannot fake green gates
risk: A package gate can print success without reading files or running a validator.
mustFailWhen: A check, scan check, verify, test, or build check script is empty or only runs echo success, echo ok, exit 0, or true.

items.title: Covered matrix entries require real tests
risk: A risk item can be marked covered without a test file or source evidence.
mustFailWhen: A required matrix contract is deleted; a covered item changes its governance owner, verification change, gate, required tests, sources, or checker binding; its gate does not execute the bound checker; or a required test file lacks a real test declaration.

items.title: CI green is not release ready
risk: A GitHub Actions pass can be reported as release readiness without separate release and runtime evidence.
mustFailWhen: Handover or verification evidence implies CI passed means release ready, or omits the separate GitHub Actions and verify:release light states.

items.title: Runtime acceptance is separate from local green
risk: Local governance checks can be mistaken for API, browser, database, or manual acceptance evidence.
mustFailWhen: Verification or handover omits runtime acceptance state, infers acceptance from npm run check, or fails to name API, browser, DB, or manual evidence.

items.title: beforeSalesOrder blocks runtime bypass
risk: Sales-order runtime files, routes, SQL, menus, permissions, or bypass-capable RuoYi roots can be created before the gate opens.
mustFailWhen: A change creates sales-order runtime artifacts while beforeSalesOrder is blocked.

items.title: High-risk permissions must close to real sources
risk: High-risk permission coverage can drift from real API, permission, or registry sources.
mustFailWhen: A required high-risk customer fund API is missing required coverage, permission metadata, or source closure.

items.title: Validation SQL must depend on real owned tables
risk: Validation SQL can include stale table checks or customer checks for platform-owned tables.
mustFailWhen: Customer validation SQL reintroduces idempotent_request or references a table that is not generated in the database scan.

items.title: UI graph screens must come from real source files
risk: The UI graph can become green with fake screens or empty file paths.
mustFailWhen: graph/ui-graph.json contains a screen with an empty file path or a source file that does not exist.

items.title: API graph must carry permission source
risk: API graph entries can be treated as covered without permission metadata from real source.
mustFailWhen: An API graph entry that requires permission governance lacks a permission field or points at missing source.

items.title: Forbidden edit roots override allowed edit roots
risk: A forbidden runtime path can be allowed by a broader allowedEditRoots entry.
mustFailWhen: Boundary checks permit a changed file under forbiddenEditRoots because the same path is also under allowedEditRoots.

items.title: RuoYi business permissions map to feature ownership
risk: RuoYi business:<feature>:<action> permissions can drift away from feature ownership.
mustFailWhen: A scanned RuoYi business permission lacks a feature mapping or maps to the wrong feature owner.

items.title: Rule objects require explicit preflight identity
risk: A rule object can be added without explicit preflight identity and ownership evidence.
mustFailWhen: A rule object lacks required identity, source contract, owned file, test, ownership, or change-record references.

items.title: RuoYi legacy findings require an exact canonical hash baseline
risk: Stable imported RuoYi findings can disappear behind change-local path exceptions, or a changed file can continue borrowing an obsolete legacy exemption.
mustFailWhen: A legacy entry uses a non-canonical path, glob, or directory path; lacks a reason or full source commit; names a missing, shallow, post-base, or non-ancestor commit; points to a symlink, gitlink, invalid UTF-8 source, or sourceCommit:file whose regular-blob canonical hash differs at the source commit, impact base, or current tree; duplicates a finding; or no longer maps to the exact component check or boundary target.

items.title: Current-change exceptions require exact structured actual-file scope
risk: An active change can turn unrelated historical findings green through allow-all text, prose path mentions, wildcards, or a whole-file boundary skip.
mustFailWhen: A component or boundary exception is not a structured exact file-check or file-target entry with a reason, names a file absent from current changed-files.json or the baseRevision-bound actual Git set, uses allow-all or a wildcard, duplicates an entry, or no longer corresponds to an observed finding.

items.title: Edit and approval roots are canonical repository-relative paths
risk: Empty, root, absolute, parent-relative, duplicated-separator, or backslash roots can normalize into an allow-all scope and bypass allowed or approved edit boundaries.
mustFailWhen: Any allowedEditRoots or forbiddenEditRoots entry is empty, absolute, dot-relative, parent-relative, has dot segments, duplicate separators, backslashes, surrounding whitespace, or a trailing separator; invalid approvedEditRoots must never authorize a runtime file.

items.title: Implementation review approval binds exact revision feature and roots
risk: An unrelated, same-diff, or stale approved review can be reused to authorize a different feature, runtime module, edit root, or Git range.
mustFailWhen: A complex business change lacks impact.reviewId or a fixed full commit baseRevision, the referenced review package did not already exist at the implementation base, changes in the same Git range, lacks its own fixed baseRevision or explicit approval, has a different id or approved feature, treats a non-Markdown file under generic backend/frontend/ruoyi-ui or any RuoYi main/test source tree as non-implementation, treats a nested src/common dist or node_modules directory as generated output, omits a runtime file from approvedEditRoots, has a review base outside the impact ancestry, or lets a context override trust review.json while decision.md is not exactly Allow Implementation.

items.title: Changed-files evidence equals the exact Git range
risk: Finalized evidence can omit committed changes, generated-looking source paths, or overclaim untouched files when it is built from request text, moving revisions, impact roots, or working-tree-only observations.
mustFailWhen: impact.baseRevision is not a fixed full 40-character commit OID, rename detection collapses an old path instead of governing both delete and add paths, raw Git mode/object evidence is missing, an allowed-root change introduces a symlink or gitlink, a mode-only change is accepted as current-exception content evidence, a Git-reported base-to-worktree deleted, renamed, untracked, or generated-looking source path is absent from changed-files.json, or changed-files.json contains a file not changed since the bound base revision.

items.title: Active and memory handovers list the exact changed-file set
risk: A handover can pass with a category summary, truncated list, omitted changed file, or invented file even while changed-files.json is exact.
mustFailWhen: The active change handover or memory/HANDOVER.md lacks a parseable Changed Files section, contains anything other than one canonical backticked file bullet per line, truncates the list, duplicates a path, omits a changed-files.json path, or lists a path outside changed-files.json.

items.title: Java tests require explicit feature ownership
risk: Tests under src/test/java can exist outside the feature registry or self-add a broad exception and create untraceable or misleading runtime coverage.
mustFailWhen: A Java or Node test matches a feature but is missing from both feature tests and ownership.tests; test discovery skips target, build, tmp, dist, or node_modules below tests or src/test/java; a business-matched test is disguised as governance-test or shared-test; a cross-feature exception does not independently match at least two features or omits a matched owner; an exception names a fake or unrelated owner; a Java test matches no feature or multiple features; or a non-rule-change edits the exception registry.

items.title: Current context is deterministic and bound to active impact
risk: A hardcoded or stale context can report the wrong feature, change id, edit roots, nonexistent must-read file, or local absolute path while governance checks appear green.
mustFailWhen: current-context currentChange, registered currentFeature, allowedEditRoots, forbiddenEditRoots, generated mustReadFiles, or Markdown rendering differs from the active impact and JSON truth; a must-read path is missing, non-file, or absolute; Markdown leaks a Windows/UNC workspace path; or a focused feature override is not explicitly covered by an unchanged review package already committed at the fixed impact base.

items.title: CI requires immutable actions locked installs real tests audit and production build
risk: CI can be green after mutable third-party Action resolution, unlocked dependency resolution, compile-only Maven work, skipped tests, an implicit or missing frontend test, a weak or dependency-omitting frontend audit, or a non-production frontend build.
mustFailWhen: The workflow uses invalid YAML, a non-SHA third-party Action or reusable-workflow reference, a non-digest Docker image, an escaped YAML key that bypasses semantic parsing, a custom or inherited verification shell, a dependency-skippable needs job, or a shallow checkout while historical baselines exist; mutates GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_PATH before fixed verification; counts strategy/matrix data, heredoc/string/function/conditional/subshell text, or any non-dedicated run program as executed coverage; omits root npm ci, npm test, Maven unit and integration verification, ruoyi-ui npm ci, an explicit ruoyi-ui test, one literal info/low/moderate audit with development dependencies included, or build:prod; accepts Maven environment variables that add command arguments, dynamic test options, skip flags including maven.test.skip.exec, selectors, or failure masking; accepts high, critical, missing, dynamic, duplicated, conflicting, fix, production-only, or dependency-omitting audit forms; misses an additional frontend audit hidden behind an equivalent working directory, cd/pushd options, npm or process-wrapper chain, YAML or run-block environment-resolved command, unresolved shell or Actions executable expression, dynamic npm subcommand or argument, NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX, normalized prefix, or dynamic frontend path; fails to resolve a declared repository-root environment alias before classification or conflates a known repository-root audit with frontend uniqueness; places required coverage behind a job or step condition; masks a required command failure with shell control flow, disabled errexit, an unsafe pipeline, background execution, trailing success, or any non-false continue-on-error value; uses skip-test flags or echo-only commands; or counts root npm commands as frontend coverage.

items.title: Release verification resolves Maven portably and fails fast
risk: The release gate can fail before backend integration tests on a machine whose configured Maven is not on PATH, or a wrapper can mask, duplicate, reorder, or weaken required release steps.
mustFailWhen: verify:release does not use the configured runtime-policy Maven command with standard mvn fallback; omits, duplicates, reorders, masks, or weakens governance, production safety, the exact ruoyi-business integration reactor, frontend tests, the full moderate audit including development dependencies, or the production build; or continues after any failed step.

items.title: Executable ESM helpers are scanned without becoming route pages
risk: A .mjs helper can hide API calls, permissions, cross-feature imports, sales-order runtime, feature references, deletion residue, duplicate code, or text hygiene issues while generated checks remain green.
mustFailWhen: Any non-route code, API, permission, component-consumer, ownership, boundary, phase-gate, impact, orphan, removal, duplicate, file-weight, or text-hygiene traversal omits .mjs; or route/component-page discovery reclassifies a plain .mjs helper as a screen or component candidate.

items.title: Phase-gate content scanning distinguishes executable files from Markdown
risk: Scanning governance Markdown as runtime code creates false blockers and encourages broad exceptions that could then hide real sales-order implementation.
mustFailWhen: An incomplete beforeSalesOrder gate permits sales-order paths or content in executable Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Vue, SQL, XML, properties, YAML, or Kotlin files, while Markdown ownership and governance prose must remain non-runtime evidence.

items.title: Runtime verification executes one aggregate Maven reactor
risk: Running the root Maven reactor and its child modules independently duplicates work, can produce inconsistent evidence, and can hide which aggregate result governs readiness.
mustFailWhen: Runtime project detection schedules child Maven modules separately after a root reactor pom declares them, or executable runtime verification invokes more than one aggregate Maven run for that reactor.
